correctness.rationale: Adjacent ruler symbols differ, so palindromes have integral centers c. The maximal radius is 2^v_2(c)-1: for 0<d<2^v_2(c) both reflected valuations equal v_2(d), and at the next distance the reflected valuations differ or the left endpoint is zero. Thus the suffixes of the prefix ending at n are exactly the truncations c obtained by retaining any chosen set bit i and zeroing below it. The preceding length m_i = n-2(n mod 2^i)-1 flips bits 0 through i. In the run count (adjacent transitions including the leading zero, but no trailing zero), only the boundary (i+1,i) changes. Each suffix step lowers the count by one exactly when bit i+1 is zero. The highest set bit is always available, proving the length formula by induction and selecting precisely the most-significant bit of each one-run as an optimal final cut. These disjoint cut classes give M_r=ceil(r/2) M_{r-1} with M_0=1 and the claimed factorials. The histogram is the sum of binom(ell-1,r-1) over r<=ell<=m; strict growth above r=2 yields the unique alternating m-bit maximizer for m>=3. Independent literal center expansion and exact cut DP (independent_ruler_check.py) checked 24,576 palindrome occurrences and the counts and final-cut sets at all 4,095 nonempty prefixes below 2^12, as well as the histogram and maximizer there. This is finite corroboration only. The frozen verify.py was inspected, not executed; its 16 histogram bins are at one cutoff, not 16 independently checked cutoffs.

evidence: Li's Proposition 2 is an if-and-only-if about every palindrome suffix via an allowed binary mask, not just one greedy cut. Theorem 1 gives the minimum-length function for every predecessor. Fici et al. count all suffixes by popcount, not the optimal ones.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Li's two statements together give all outgoing cuts and their optimum status at every prefix. The additive one on each letter does not affect equality of symbols; no change of input class blocks the deduction. The suffix-count lemma alone would not suffice.

evidence: Li's mask flips the suffix of the binary representation beginning at a set bit. Flipping this suffix leaves all internal adjacent comparisons unchanged, so the run count drops iff the bit at the mask boundary begins a one-run. Exactly ceil(r/2) cuts lead to rank r-1. The standard optimal-cut DP therefore has a rank-only recurrence.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The mechanical implication does not rely on a conjecture about which cuts occur, nor on future calculations. The binomial distribution then follows by choosing transition positions in ordinary binary strings; the alternating maximizer is its immediate extremal case.

evidence: The indexed Finding (offset 0) gives the same all-n count in terms of popcount(n xor floor(n/2)), exactly the binary run count. Its count includes the empty factorization and distinguishes cut lists. Its proof (offset 3860) gives the same recurrence via Gray flips.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The Gray-code description is a bijective re-expression, not a different invariant. Choosing the last admissible Gray position from the final bit set means choosing one of the positions with an even number of larger set bits; under inverse Gray this is the high end of a one-run. This is substantive exact overlap independently of date order.

value.rationale: Counting optimal factorizations of a canonical infinite word is a natural question, but the principal invariant adds no distinct result given the exact overlap and the direct earlier mask-to-DP deduction. The residual histogram is the ordinary binary run-count binomial identity, and the alternating maximizer is its immediate consequence. No nonroutine and separately useful remainder warrants a repair.
